axis_detail: metal ions (catalytic Fe/Cu present vs removed)
window_type_basis: Evidence: in catalytic-metal-free, air-saturated pH 7 buffer ascorbate did not autoxidise (loss below detection), i.e. NECESSARY in that model system. Encoded MODULATING: the MECH schema treats metal ions as CATALYST modifiers (MODULATING gate, rule M-1), and a metal-free medium is not a cooking condition; a NECESSARY gate would turn the usual UNKNOWN metal input into UNKNOWN for every AA oxidation (H4, D21-20).
direction_of_effect: trace Fe/Cu catalyse AA autoxidation; removing them suppresses it below detection
matrix_scope: aqueous buffer, pH 7.0, air-saturated, catalytic metals removed (not a food)
time_qualifier: first-order loss constant < 6 x 10^-7 s^-1 at pH 7.0 (upper limit)
source_citation: Buettner GR (1988) In the absence of catalytic metals ascorbate does not autoxidize at pH 7: ascorbate as a test for catalytic metals. J Biochem Biophys Methods 16(1):27-40

Lane arithmetic (not in source): k < 6e-7 s^-1 means t1/2 > ~13 days. Only pH 7 is covered by the abstract.
